Aug. 2 (UPI) -- The suspect in a deadly mass shooting at an Idaho burger restaurant died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound, authorities said in an update issued Sunday.

The alleged shooter, identified as Chad Williams, 24, died by suicide following the Saturday afternoon incident at the In-N-Out Burger in Twin Falls, Idaho, Police Chief Matthew Hicks said at a news conference.

Based on current information, three people died and seven others were injured in the shooting, two of whom remain in critical condition, the chief said.

None of their identities were immediately released.

Hicks denied rumors that there were more than one shooter, asserting Williams acted alone, and revealed that the presence of an off-duty law enforcement officer at the restaurant may have prevented more people from dying.

"We can confirm that there was an off-duty state trooper and a citizen who actively engaged the suspect by returning gunfire towards him," he said.

"We want to take a moment and commend the actions of the off-duty officer and the citizen and their heroic action to stop this incident. We believe their actions helped drive the suspect away from the scene, preventing further casualties."



freestar.config.enabled_slots.push({ placementName: "upi-com_incontent_reusable", slotId: "upi-com_incontent_reusable_64792" });

No motive for the attack has yet been established and police are "still working to determine the full set of circumstances in this incident, including the suspect's actions and possible motivations," the chief added.

Williams' family is cooperating with the investigation and authorities pleaded with the public to submit any additional evidence or information they may have.

"I want to tell the citizens of Twin Falls how proud they should be of the men and women of law enforcement and their first responders and how they responded to this incident and the bravery they displayed yesterday," Hicks said.

"Together our community will get through this."

Police said they responded to reports of shots fired in a busy commercial area of Twin Falls about 2:30 p.m. on Saturday and upon arriving at the restaurant encountered what Hicks called "one of the most chaotic instances a law enforcement officer can face in their career."

Videos posted on social media showed a man wearing a black shirt and carrying a large rifle in the area, Boise State Public Radio reported.

The man reportedly shot the front windshield of a parked car and later walked into the In-N-Out drive-through.
